rhs_question_text:
A computer in a design office uses several CPU components and registers.

rhs_verified_answer_points: PC; CU coordinates/control or decodes instructions; MAR; ALU.

rhs_question_text:
Visitors at a museum use its network simultaneously to view digital exhibits.

Explain why a growing number of active devices may reduce network performance. [3]
original_question_summary: Explain simultaneous devices and network performance
rhs_verified_answer_points: More concurrent traffic; shared bandwidth means less is available per active device; slower transfers/waiting/latency/retransmissions.
rhs_verified_marking_rule: Up to 3 distinct valid points; do not say total network bandwidth itself decreases.
rhs_answer_review_notes: Compared RHS assessment demand and answer with June 2022 OCR J277/01 paper and mark scheme.

rhs_question_text:
A museum's network becomes slow during busy periods.

Identify one factor other than the number of connected devices that could affect its performance. [1]
original_question_summary: Identify another factor affecting performance
rhs_verified_answer_points: Bandwidth, interference, medium, transmission data, network hardware, distance, topology or error rate.
rhs_verified_marking_rule: 1 distinct factor; do not repeat device count.
rhs_answer_review_notes: Compared RHS assessment demand and answer with June 2022 OCR J277/01 paper and mark scheme.

rhs_question_text:
A community theatre lets guests visit its website.

Complete seven gaps using terms from this word bank (not every term will be used): web server, file server, clients, routers, Uniform Resource Locator, Domain Name Server, 0, 1, 255, 256, colon, full stop.

(1) A site is hosted on a ___. (2) A visiting computer is a ___. (3) A person enters a ___ into the browser. (4) The browser can request a matching IP address from a ___. (5–6) IPv4 octets use values from ___ to ___ inclusive. (7) The octets are separated by a ___. [7]
original_question_summary: Complete website access and IPv4 terminology
rhs_verified_answer_points: Web server; clients; Uniform Resource Locator; Domain Name Server; 0; 255; full stop.
rhs_verified_marking_rule: 1 per correct gap; original supplies a word bank, RHS draft needs one to match support.
rhs_answer_review_notes: Detected RHS scenario or format problem; revised RHS question to preserve available original marks and answer structure; check against live question layout before classroom use.

rhs_question_text:
A recording studio uses Ethernet connections between its computers.

Explain why Ethernet is regarded as a networking standard. [2]
original_question_summary: Explain why Ethernet is a standard
rhs_verified_answer_points: Widely adopted by manufacturers; ensures compatibility; reliable/proven; inexpensive to install/use; other valid features.
rhs_verified_marking_rule: Up to 2 independent credited reasons.
rhs_answer_review_notes: Compared RHS assessment demand and answer with June 2022 OCR J277/01 paper and mark scheme.

rhs_question_text:
A café's network uses a router to communicate with other networks.

Identify three different tasks that the router performs when handling network traffic. [3]
rhs_marking_guidance: Examples include receiving packets; forwarding packets; keeping a routing table; choosing a route; assigning IP addresses; or translating between protocols.
original_question_summary: Identify three router tasks
rhs_verified_answer_points: Receives packets; forwards packets; maintains a routing table; chooses path; assigns addresses; translates protocols.
rhs_verified_marking_rule: Any 3 distinct router tasks, not just broad use/purpose.
rhs_answer_review_notes: Compared RHS assessment demand and answer with June 2022 OCR J277/01 paper and mark scheme.

rhs_question_text:
An office transmits confidential files across its network.

Give two reasons why the organisation should encrypt data before transmission. [2]
original_question_summary: Reasons for network encryption
rhs_verified_answer_points: Intercepted encrypted data cannot be understood; protects personal or confidential information; may meet legal obligations.
rhs_verified_marking_rule: 1 for each of 2 independent reasons relating to data transmission.
rhs_answer_review_notes: Compared RHS assessment demand and answer with June 2022 OCR J277/01 paper and mark scheme.

rhs_question_text:
Staff at a sports centre use a network to send messages and visit secure websites.

Identify an appropriate protocol for (a) sending email and (b) accessing a secure web page. [2]
original_question_summary: Email and secure-web protocols
rhs_verified_answer_points: SMTP for sending email; HTTPS for securely accessing a website.
rhs_verified_marking_rule: 1 per matching protocol.
rhs_answer_review_notes: Compared RHS assessment demand and answer with June 2022 OCR J277/01 paper and mark scheme.

rhs_question_text:
A social media platform used by a college employs artificial intelligence to monitor user posts.

Discuss the potential consequences of using AI to monitor activity on social networking websites. Consider more than one viewpoint. [8]
original_question_summary: Discuss AI monitoring on social networking websites
rhs_verified_answer_points: Balanced argument about automatic monitoring of posts: privacy/consent, incorrect blocks, safeguarding, copyright, legal requirements and security.
rhs_verified_marking_rule: Level of response: 1–2 limited; 3–5 reasonable; 6–8 thorough, balanced, contextual and justified.
rhs_answer_review_notes: Compared RHS assessment demand and answer with June 2022 OCR J277/01 paper and mark scheme.

rhs_question_text:
A small museum is improving access to its computers.

Identify two physical security measures it could introduce. [2]

rhs_verified_answer_points: Locks; access cards/passcodes; controlled-room biometrics; alarms; CCTV; guards.
rhs_verified_marking_rule: 1 per distinct physical measure; passwords for logging into software do not count.
rhs_answer_review_notes: Compared RHS assessment demand and answer with June 2022 OCR J277/01 paper and mark scheme.

rhs_question_text:
An office wants to protect its computers and files against unauthorised access.

Identify and describe two different software-based security methods that the office could implement. [6]
original_question_summary: Describe software-based security methods
rhs_verified_answer_points: Two distinct software measures such as anti-malware, firewall, encryption, authentication or user access levels, each with meaningful operation.
rhs_verified_marking_rule: 3 marks per method: 1 naming, up to 2 valid description points. RHS wording must explicitly ask for two.
rhs_answer_review_notes: Detected RHS scenario or format problem; revised RHS question to preserve available original marks and answer structure; check against live question layout before classroom use.

rhs_question_text:
A library wants staff to recognise when computer laws apply.

For each situation, identify the relevant legislation: (1) customer details passed to another firm without a legal basis; (2) a visitor's private address accidentally displayed online; (3) a rival copies a paid application's original graphics; (4) a person uses another staff member's unlocked computer without permission; (5) an employee guesses a colleague's password to access their account. Choose between the Data Protection Act 2018, Computer Misuse Act 1990 and Copyright, Designs and Patents Act 1988. [5]
original_question_summary: Match scenarios to legislation
rhs_verified_answer_points: Data Protection Act 2018; Data Protection Act 2018; Copyright, Designs and Patents Act 1988; Computer Misuse Act 1990; Computer Misuse Act 1990.
rhs_verified_marking_rule: 1 appropriate law per scenario, max 5.
rhs_answer_review_notes: Compared RHS assessment demand and answer with June 2022 OCR J277/01 paper and mark scheme.

rhs_question_text:
A podcast producer records interviews using a microphone.

Describe how the analogue sound signal is turned into a digital recording. [3]
original_question_summary: Describe analogue sound digitisation
rhs_verified_answer_points: Sample analogue signal amplitude at regular intervals; encode measured amplitudes as binary values stored in order.
rhs_verified_marking_rule: Up to 3 distinct stages. Measuring frequency instead of amplitude is not creditworthy.
rhs_answer_review_notes: Compared RHS assessment demand and answer with June 2022 OCR J277/01 paper and mark scheme.

rhs_question_text:
A radio station changes a recording. For each change, select every effect that applies from: file size increases, file size decreases, accuracy increases, accuracy decreases.

(a) Duration increases from 10 to 20 minutes. (b) Sample rate falls from 44 kHz to 8 kHz. (c) Bit depth rises from 8 to 16 bits. [3]
original_question_summary: Effects of duration sample rate and bit depth
rhs_verified_answer_points: Longer duration → larger file; lower sampling rate → smaller file and reduced accuracy; higher bit depth → larger file and greater accuracy.
rhs_verified_marking_rule: 1 correct selection per row (potentially multiple effects in a row). RHS draft needs a clear multi-select answer table.
rhs_answer_review_notes: Detected RHS scenario or format problem; revised RHS question to preserve available original marks and answer structure; check against live question layout before classroom use.

rhs_answer_review_notes: Compared RHS assessment demand and answer with June 2022 OCR J277/01 paper and mark scheme.

rhs_question_text:

rhs_answer_review_notes: Compared RHS assessment demand and answer with June 2022 OCR J277/01 paper and mark scheme.

rhs_question_text:
An airport information display plays announcements and shows travel videos.

Give two examples of data it could hold in RAM while operating. [2]

An airport information display also contains secondary storage.

rhs_answer_review_notes: Checked against official OCR 2022 J277/02 question paper and marking scheme; RHS guidance separately authored.

rhs_answer_review_notes: Checked against official OCR 2022 J277/02 question paper and marking scheme; RHS guidance separately authored.

rhs_question_text:
